why: The Magog route page and the area page describe an approach toward Friendship Col and the remains of the Echo Glacier but say nothing on crevasses, and the area page calls the terrain glacial.
The route page crosses what is left of the Echo Glacier snowfield to a moat and gives no word on crevasses or roping, so the question stays open.
Area pages and an old journal note read give no approach for this line, so nothing could be settled.
The route page describes the approach as cols, boulders, snow and scree with no glacier named, but it passes the Crescent col area where the Crescent Glacier lies, so crevassed ice is not ruled out.
The area page has the approach pass the remnants of the Crescent Glacier and a descent by hiking, with no mention of snow, axes or crampons, so the snow question is not settled.

The Mountain Project area page puts this 5.10d line on granite walls reached by an easy trail in Cathedral Park, and a club wiki says the park avoids glacier travel; snow is only a warning about slopes.
The area page lists only a steep snow tag and the shared forest and slide-path approach, with no description of this couloir.
Pages on the Battle Range call it very glaciated and tag the route steep snow, but none describes the north ridge approach.
Wikipedia puts unnamed glaciers on the north and east slopes, and the west-ridge trip report avoids the glacier, but no page I could read describes the east ridge itself.
Wikipedia places glaciers on the west, south-east and north slopes and no readable page describes this arete.
An American Alpine Journal report of the north-east ridge has a hike from camp, snow arets and a gully descent with no glacier crossing, but nothing confirms it is this named line.
